## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design tenant-scoped observability without touching production logs, using a lightweight sidecar, and ConfigMap-driven routing.

## Key Concepts
- Fluent Bit routing per-namespace
- NamespaceConfigMap as policy store
- Tenant isolation and auditability
- Minimal in-cluster validation

## Code Example
```yaml
# NamespaceConfigMap example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-logging-config
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  tenantID: "tenant-a"
  sinkURL: "http://log-sink-a:24224"
```

```yaml
# sidecar snippet concept (pseudo, for illustration)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnf-logging-sidecar
spec:
  containers:
  - name: sidecar
    image: cnf/sidecar:latest
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: tenant-logging-config
```

```bash
# minimal validation
kubectl apply -f tenant-a.yaml
kubectl apply -f tenant-b.yaml
kubectl logs -l app=cnf-logging-sidecar -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle sink failures or backpressure?
- How would you audit cross-tenant log access?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement tenant-scoped feature gating, combining CRDs, policy-as-code, and canary-style risk mitigation in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- FeatureGate CRD and TenantFeatureGate per-tenant
- OPA Gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Path-based canary gating and per-tenant isolation
- Minimal YAML for CRD, policy, namespace, and a basic test

## Code Example
```yaml
# FeatureGate CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featuregates.example.org
spec:
  group: example.org
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featuregates
    singular: featuregate
    kind: FeatureGate
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (OPA)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sfeaturegate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sFeatureGate
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sfeaturegate
        violation["deny"] {
          input.target.path == "/v1/beta"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["tenant/feature-v1-beta"] == "enabled"
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-tenant)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sFeatureGate
metadata:
  name: tenant-v1beta-enabled
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["gateway.example.org"]
        kinds: ["GatewayRoute"]
  parameters:
    # feature flag key used in tenant annotation
    flagKey: "tenant/feature-v1-beta"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest enabling the flag
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    tenant/feature-v1-beta: enabled
```

```bash
# quick test (pseudo)
curl -H "Host: gateway.example.org" https://gateway/health
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical traffic shaping, per-tenant configuration, and end-to-end validation in CNF gateways. It favors deterministic routing to avoid flapping and shows how to wire a ConfigMap-driven control plane into a sidecar.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant canary rollout
- Deterministic routing via hashing
- Namespace-scoped ConfigMap as control plane

## Code Example
```javascript
function shouldCanary(tenantID, path, canaryEnabled, percent) {
  if (!canaryEnabled) return false;
  const h = hash(tenantID + path) // 32-bit
  return (h % 100) < percent;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor rollout progress and rollback if issues arise?
- How would you handle multi-namespace deployments with shared upstreams?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests design of scalable edge enforcement using in-kernel routing (eBPF) and Kubernetes operators, a realistic CNF ops pattern across regions.

## Key Concepts
- CustomResourceDefinition design for per-tenant network policy
- Kubernetes controller reconciliation to reflect CRD state into eBPF maps
- Sidecar-based map loading and hot-reload without downtime
- Rollout strategies, observability, and fault-tolerance

## Code Example
```yaml
# CRD: TenantNetworkPolicy
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantnetworkpolicies.example.net
spec:
  group: example.net
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              rateLimit:
                type: integer
              allowedCIDR:
                type: string
              blockedPorts:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: integer
```
```yaml
# Tenant example (t8)
apiVersion: example.net/v1
kind: TenantNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: t8
spec:
  tenantID: t8
  rateLimit: 100
  allowedCIDR: 10.1.0.0/16
  blockedPorts: [22]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle conflicting policies from multiple controllers or regions?
- What are the failure modes during map reloads and how do you mitigate them?

      names:
        kind: CNFImageVuln
      scope: Cluster

      package cnfimagevuln
      violation[{"msg": msg}]

        vul := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["image.vulns"];

func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {

}
